chapter: Benny Carter, saxophones and Coleman Hawkins's last years
title: Benny Carter's dignified manner and the nickname King
summary: Carter was always straightforward and dignified; Dickie Wells called him King because he played so much alto.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, I mean you knew Benny when he was quite young. I mean did Benny Carter always have that sort of dignified manner, or did he acquire that?
No, he was always a very straightforward fellow.

Yeah, Roy was straightforward, straight, you know, and very dignified. We used to -- we're very good friends, kid a lot. I'd say -- we used to call him -- call him King. I mean Dickie Wells started to call him King. 'Hey, King, what you going to play tonight?' Cut out that. 'Hey, King, come on, we go ahead and get a little cutting -- cut each other. Let's get a little cutting session.
When he'd call him King -- I mean why did he call him King?
He played so much alto. He wasn't playing the trumpet then, but he liked the trumpet later. Oh, after his cousin came there, then naturally he played the trumpet.
